notes: Q4 FY2026 print (reported 2026-07-29 after close, quarter ended 2026-06-30): revenue $90.0B beat the ~$87.6B Street estimate by 2.7%, GAAP diluted EPS $4.81 (+32% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $4.74 beat by ~11.8%. Azure accelerated to 43% YoY (from Q3's 40%), crossed $100B in full-year revenue for the first time, and management guided Q1 FY2027 to ~45% growth in constant currency -- both the actual print AND the forward guide individually clear the OLD bull-case threshold of 'Azure beats 41%+', which is the single biggest development this quarter: the deceleration bear case that anchored this thesis since April is now falsified by two consecutive quarters of acceleration, not deceleration. Copilot paid seats more than doubled sequentially to 30M+ (from Q3's 20M). BUT in the same release, Microsoft guided FY2027 capex to $255-260B -- up sharply from FY2026's already-large $190B -- pushing the capex/revenue ratio from ~56% toward an estimated ~65%. Free cash flow fell to $19.6B in Q4 on the capex ramp. Microsoft also extended data center/office useful life from 15 to 25 years starting FY2027 and reclassified new DC leases from finance to operating treatment -- a real but partly cosmetic tailwind to near-term reported margins/EPS via lower depreciation, worth flagging as an accounting change rather than a fundamental improvement. Stock reaction: +15.5% on 2026-07-30 (from $390.54 pre-print close to $451.10), but even after that pop the price sits below the OLD base-band floor of $460 that existed going into this print -- the market appears to be pricing the beat against the much larger capex number, not against the pre-print bands. Pull-forward test: management's framing (Azure crossing $100B, capacity commentary implied by the growth acceleration itself) reads as durable demand extending the runway rather than pull-forward, but the true test is whether Q1 FY27's guided 45% actually prints, and whether FCF stabilizes as a share of revenue once the FY2027 capex ramp is underway -- named as the explicit bear-case kill zone going forward. AI Business ARR was NOT re-disclosed on the Q4 call in available coverage -- carried forward at the stale $37B/Q3 figure rather than fabricated, flagged in SIGNALS as 'not updated Q4', watch for a fresh number on the Q1 FY27 call. Peer median forward P/E (~22x across GOOGL/META/AMZN) is essentially unchanged from the pre-print regime, meaning this was an earnings-driven repricing specific to MSFT, not a group re-rating -- own-history anchoring alone would have missed that distinction.
